evidence_added: checkpoint_retention {keep_every K, keep_last M>=2} declared in RUN_MANIFEST (null = keep all); retention.prune keeps genesis, every Kth, last M (head and its input), and k/k-1 of any recorded contest; deletes only checkpoint objects no chain keeps; worker prunes after each head advance; CLI prune [--dry-run]; each pass logged to partitions/<chain>/retention.jsonl

fire test TestFireAfterPruning: worker crashed at head 9 after epochs 1-3,5-7 pruned; forced s3.8 replay VALID; resumed to 12; final forced replay VALID; run digest == control; pruned run stores fewer bytes than the unpruned run

red_observed.detail: tests written first and run against the missing module (ImportError); tests and code were committed together, so RED is not a separate commit

known_escapes: a contest recorded after its epoch was pruned cannot restore the checkpoint (M>=2 keeps every epoch a fresh contest can name)
the runner records no contest resolution, so every recorded contest counts as open
orphan checkpoints of refused publications are not pruned
single host local store only; full 17-mutant table not re-run (only the 4 new retention mutants)
unblocks: C-013-T025 shares the runner tree and follows in order

resources.cpu: test suites and mutants ~6 CPU-min (< 0.2 core-hour)

notes: No OS scheduler task, no Fabric restart. Design and policy semantics in rso/scale/runner/RETENTION.md.
